data.one_liner: Check if the app is running for the first time.
data.what_it_does: Provides methods to check if it is the first time the app runs or the first time a specific method is called. It relies internally on shared_preferences to persist the state. It also offers a reset function to clear the recorded state.
use_when: You want to show an onboarding walkthrough on the first app launch
You need to trigger a one-time migration or setup task on the initial run
avoid_when: You already manage persistent preferences and want to minimize dependency overhead by implementing the check directly
strengths: Supports all major Flutter platforms (Android, iOS, Web, Windows, macOS, Linux)
weaknesses: Relies on shared_preferences, which may not be suitable if you require encrypted storage
Limited functionality beyond checking the first run state

alternatives.name: shared_preferences
alternatives.why_pick_it: Allows you to implement first-run checks manually while gaining full control over all stored key-value preferences.
